parts.title: Sign, Baby, Sign!
parts.article:
Sign, Baby, Sign!
 
(A) Language is a powerful tool that humans use for a wide variety of purposes—from expressing emotions and sharing ideas to passing down cultural values and acquiring knowledge. It is not limited to spoken words; gestures, facial expressions, and even posture all contribute to how we communicate. Language, whether signed or spoken, plays a vital role in how we engage with the world around us.
 
(B) In recent years, many American schools have begun to recognize American Sign Language (ASL) as a valid foreign language credit, just like Spanish or French. This change has opened the door for hearing students to choose ASL as an academic subject, which not only gives them a practical skill but also increases their awareness of and empathy toward the Deaf community. Some educators believe this early exposure may even influence students to pursue careers in special education, speech therapy, or interpreting.
 
(C) One clear benefit of learning ASL for hearing children is the opportunity for broader social interaction. Children who understand ASL can communicate with deaf peers, making their social circles more inclusive. Additionally, they may find it easier to express complex ideas or emotions non-verbally, which is helpful in noisy environments or when verbal speech isn't possible.
 
(D) Dr. Marilyn Daniels, a researcher and advocate for baby sign language, has spent over two decades studying the impact of signing on early communication. While she promotes the use of sign language with infants, she emphasizes that there is no need for parents to invent their own signs. Instead, she suggests that parents use ASL or another standardized system to ensure consistency and eventual recognition by others.
 
(E) Very young children often develop motor skills before verbal skills. Dr. Daniels notes that even babies as young as six months can learn to use simple signs like “milk” or “more” with their hands, long before they can articulate those words. This early form of communication can reduce frustration—for both babies and their parents—and may even accelerate speech development.
 
(F) Studies have shown that hearing children exposed to sign language from an early age tend to have stronger reading skills by the time they enter primary school. It is believed that learning sign language can strengthen understanding of symbolic representation and grammar, both of which are foundational to literacy. These cognitive advantages suggest that signing benefits not only communication but academic success as well.
 
(G) There remains some debate about the best approach to language instruction for deaf children. Some educators argue that speech and lip-reading should come first, while others advocate for immediate exposure to sign language. Dr. Daniels believes the latter is more effective and less frustrating for the child. She calls the idea that children must learn to lip-read before learning sign language “an outdated notion.” She, along with other advocates, stresses that deaf children have a right to a full, accessible language from birth—and that language is often sign.
parts.questions:
Questions 27–33
Reading Passage 3 has seven paragraphs, A-G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?
Write the correct letter, A-G, in boxes 27–33 on your answer sheet.
NB You may use any letter more than once.

Q27 A statement about the different things people use language for

  • A
  • B
  • C
  • D
  • E
  • F
  • G

Q28 How knowing ASL may benefit students in their future subject choices

Q29 An assertion that deaf children have a right to be taught a sign language

Q30 An observation regarding the ability of small children to use their hands

Q31 The advantage for hearing children of knowing ASL for wider social interaction

Q32 Different views on when deaf children should be taught to speak

Q33 An observation about the reading ability of primary-school-age hearing children who have been taught ASL

Questions 34–40
Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 3?
In boxes 34–40 on your answer sheet, write:

Q34 Dr. Daniels believes that parents should make up their own gestures to communicate with their babies.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q35 American Sign Language is the most widely used sign language in the world.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q36 For hearing children in America, learning American Sign Language is an equivalent option to learning a foreign language.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q37 Brain research indicates that vocabulary is more easily learned than grammar.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q38 First and second languages are stored on different sides of the brain.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q39 Children have less difficulty learning to make signs than learning to make sounds.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q40 According to Dr. Daniels, the view that deaf children must learn lip-reading before sign language is old-fashioned.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q27

干扰 “Different things people use language for” 对应原文的一系列并列动名词短语。

句子 (Paragraph A) “Language is a powerful tool... for a wide variety of purposes—from expressing emotions and sharing ideas...”

解析 题目提到关于人们使用语言的不同用途的陈述。A段开头列举了语言用于“expressing emotions... sharing ideas... passing down cultural values... acquiring knowledge（表达情感、分享观点、传承文化、获取知识）”等多种用途，选 A。

Q28

解析 题目问了解ASL如何有益于学生未来的学科/职业选择。B段提到早期接触可能影响学生“pursue careers in special education, speech therapy, or interpreting（从事特殊教育、言语治疗或口译的职业）”，选 B。

干扰 “Benefit... future subject choices” 对应原文的 “influence students to pursue careers...”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...influence students to pursue careers in special education, speech therapy, or interpreting.”

Q29

解析 题目是一个断言：聋哑儿童有权被教授手语。G段末尾提到Daniels和其他倡导者强调“deaf children have a right to a full, accessible language... and that language is often sign（聋哑儿童有权获得一种完整的、可获取的语言——即手语）”，选 G。

干扰 关键词 “right to be taught” 对应原文的 “have a right to...”。

句子 (Paragraph G) “She... stresses that deaf children have a right to a full, accessible language from birth...”

Q30

干扰 “Ability... use their hands” 对应原文的 “develop motor skills... use simple signs... with their hands”。

解析 题目提到关于幼儿使用双手能力的观察。E段提到婴儿早在能说话前就能“use simple signs... with their hands（用手做简单的手势）”，因为运动技能先于语言技能发展，选 E。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...babies as young as six months can learn to use simple signs... with their hands...”

Q31

解析 题目提到听力正常儿童学习ASL在更广泛社交互动方面的优势。C段开头明确指出“One clear benefit... is the opportunity for broader social interaction（更广泛的社交互动）”，选 C。

干扰 “Wider social interaction” 也就是原文的 “broader social interaction”，完全同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph C) “One clear benefit... is the opportunity for broader social interaction.”

Q32

解析 题目提到关于聋哑儿童何时应该被教导说话的不同观点。G段开头提到一些教育者认为“speech and lip-reading should come first（说话和唇读应优先）”，而另一些人主张立即接触手语，存在先后顺序的争议，选 G。

干扰 “Different views on when” 对应原文的争论（debate）：是先说话（come first）还是先手语（immediate exposure）。

句子 (Paragraph G) “Some educators argue that speech and lip-reading should come first, while others advocate...”

Q33

句子 (Paragraph F) “...tend to have stronger reading skills by the time they enter primary school.”

解析 题目提到关于学过ASL的小学年龄段听力正常儿童阅读能力的观察。F段提到早期接触手语的孩子在进入小学时往往有“stronger reading skills（更强的阅读技能）”，选 F。

干扰 “Reading ability” 对应原文的 “reading skills”。

Q34

解析 题目说Daniels认为家长应该**自创（make up）**手势与婴儿交流。D段原文说她强调“there is no need for parents to invent their own signs（没必要自创）”，建议使用ASL等标准系统，题目与原文相反，选 FALSE。

干扰 “Make up” = “invent”，原文明确否定了这一做法（no need）。

句子 (Paragraph D) “...she emphasizes that there is no need for parents to invent their own signs.”

Q35

解析 题目说ASL是世界上使用最广泛的手语。文中只提到美国学校认可ASL，并没有将其与世界其他手语的使用范围进行比较（most widely used），信息缺失，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 不要因为ASL很出名就默认它是世界第一，雅思只看原文证据。

Q36

解析 题目说对于美国听力正常儿童，学习ASL是学习外语的同等选项。B段提到学校认可ASL为“valid foreign language credit, just like Spanish or French（就像西班牙语或法语一样的有效外语学分）”，即地位同等，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Equivalent option” 对应原文的 “valid... credit, just like...”。

句子 (Paragraph B) “...recognize ASL as a valid foreign language credit, just like Spanish or French.”

Q37

干扰 文中提到了“vocabulary（symbolic）”和“grammar”，但没有比较难易度。

解析 题目说大脑研究表明词汇比语法更容易学。F段虽提到手语能加强对“symbolic representation and grammar”的理解，但并未比较两者谁更容易学，也未提及相关的“brain research（脑科学研究）”，选 NOT GIVEN。

句子 (Paragraph F) “...strengthen understanding of symbolic representation and grammar...” (无比较)

Q38

解析 题目说第一语言和第二语言存储在大脑的不同半球。全文未提及语言在大脑中的存储位置或左右半球的分工，选 NOT GIVEN。

干扰 文中没有涉及神经解剖学（brain sides）的具体信息。

Q39

解析 题目说儿童学习做手势比学习发声困难更小。E段提到儿童通常先发展运动技能（motor skills）后发展语言技能（verbal skills），能使用简单手势的时间“long before（远早于）”能清晰发音的时间，暗示做手势更容易/更早掌握，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Less difficulty” 可以从 “develop... before” 和 “long before they can articulate” 推导出来（先会的通常是更容易的/门槛更低的）。

句子 (Paragraph E) “...develop motor skills before verbal skills... use simple signs... long before they can articulate those words.”

Q40

解析 题目说Daniels认为聋哑儿童必须先学唇读再学手语的观点是过时的。G段说她称这种观点为“an outdated notion（一个过时的观念）”，选 TRUE。

干扰 “Old-fashioned” 是 “outdated” 的同义替换。

句子 (Paragraph G) “She calls the idea... 'an outdated notion.'”
